Syspro remains your system of record: Customers, stock, lots and invoices all stay in Syspro. We hold the guide for each account and its prices, which your team updates in our admin platform, and we keep every order a chef sends through the app.

Accounts that send POs keep sending them: Where accounts already send POs for Syspro's AI to read, leave that in place. We built the app for kitchens whose chef would rather call than write. Phoned orders get no number from us; app orders each get their own.
Portal users can stay on the portal: Kitchens happy to type into Syspro's portal can keep doing so, tracking orders and paying there. Our app is for the ones who phone you instead.

@graph.name: Do we need a Syspro alternative before kitchens can order by speaking?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Syspro keeps doing everything it does now. What VoiceOrder Solutions adds is a written, checked order from kitchens that would otherwise call you: the chef says it in our app and corrects it there, and Syspro is left as it was.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Syspro?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job only: getting a checked list of items from kitchens that never write their orders down. What Syspro does after that stays with Syspro, so we work beside it rather than in its place.

@graph.name: Doesn't Syspro already let customers order online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Its Supply Chain Portal lets customers create and track their own sales orders, see their history and pay. To use it, someone in the kitchen types each line into a website. In our app the chef just speaks the items aloud and fixes any line that is off.

@graph.name: Can't Syspro's AI handle incoming orders already?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partly. It can read a PO sent as a PDF or a photo and build the sales order from it. Syspro Torque, still in a controlled early release ahead of general availability, adds order rules that can hold a new order as a draft until it passes those checks. Both start from an order that is already written. Our app is how a kitchen that just phones produces one. Speech and AI order tools from other companies can also post orders into Syspro through its API, so we are not the only option.

@graph.name: We make product too. Does this touch production?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Recipes, batches and production remain Syspro's job, and its food pages speak to exactly that. VoiceOrder Solutions only deals with what a chef orders from you.

@graph.name: Does Syspro connect to VoiceOrder Solutions?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Each is its own product from its own company, with no link set up between them, and neither of us gives support for the software of the other. When an order travels by EDI or through the API, your desk may not need to retype it, if your Syspro setup accepts orders that way. A demo is where we find out whether yours can. If it goes by email, the attachment lists every item the kitchen checked, and someone on your desk keys it from that instead of from a call or a voicemail.

@graph.name: How quickly does it go live, and what does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It takes most distributors 24 to 48 hours, since Syspro itself stays untouched. Neither company publishes a price: Syspro lists none for its ERP, and we quote per distributor. A Syspro alternative, or any Syspro replacement, means moving the whole ERP; this leaves it where it is.

@graph.name: Where do the Syspro details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From syspro.com and Syspro's help site, as they stood on 9 November 2026: the distribution, food, sales order, customer portal, AI, Torque and implementation pages. Syspro publishes no prices, so this page states none. If you spot anything that has changed, tell us and we will fix the page.
